root_idea.summary: A semantic orientation toward strength, firmness, and constriction, extended especially to intense distress or grief.
root_idea.development: The thick, firmly tied rope-fitting of a bucket provides a concrete image of binding strength; from this branch, كَرْبٌ denotes severe grief or distress. The approach sense is treated in the lexical tradition as a k/q substitution related to قُرْب rather than as the core strength branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic noun is a distinct and recurrent lexical item meaning severe distress or affliction.

senses.usage_conditions: Quranic noun used in expressions for a distressing condition or overwhelming affliction; the form appears both indefinitely and with the definite article or in a construct phrase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be near, draw near, approach, or be on the point of doing or becoming something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes being near sunset, near maturity, near death, or near a stated quantity; the Form III usage is explicitly equated with قارَبَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind the two pasterns of an ass or camel closely together, or to tighten its shackles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use referring to fastening or narrowing an animal’s shackle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To load a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Form I transitive usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To afflict, distress, or oppress someone or something with sorrow, grief, or a distressing affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use; the object may be a person, an affair, or another matter capable of causing distress.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attach a كَرَب, a bucket-rope fitting, to a bucket.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to the rope or fastening arrangement used with a water bucket.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break, said of the rope called كَرَب belonging to a bucket.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intransitive use tied to the bucket rope.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a disputed technical expression, to make a baker’s wooden implement produce a repeated sound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The wording and interpretation are reported tentatively in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sow land of the type called كَرِيبٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural use distinct from turning or ploughing the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn over or plough the ground for sowing or cultivation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated noun denotes the turning of soil; one cited proverb uses the expression in connection with oxen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove the lower parts or ends of palm branches; to lop a palm-tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural and palm-cultivation use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat dates called كُرَابَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use referring to a named kind of date.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To twist a rope or similar object; another transmitted reading gives the meaning “to slay.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical source records conflicting readings of the verb, so the second meaning is not equally secure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause distress, sorrow, grief, or affliction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form IV use referring specifically to a skin or leather container.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To nearly fill a vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV construction expressing that the vessel has been filled almost to capacity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten, speed, or run rapidly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A marked or less usual Form IV use, especially of a person, horse, or other running animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pick the dates remaining among the roots of the branches of a palm-tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V use after the main racemes of fruit have been cut off.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become afflicted, distressed, or oppressed by sorrow, grief, or a distressing affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An inchoative or reflexive Form VIII use describing entry into a state of distress.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rope or rope-fitting attached to a bucket, including a secondary rope retained if the main rope breaks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized water-drawing implement; the exact arrangement is described somewhat differently in the lexical reports.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The thick lower parts, ends, or stumps of palm branches left after lopping.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun for the broad, step-like remains of lower palm branches.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A channel through which water flows in a valley, or an upper part of a valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular and plural are associated with valley watercourses; the lexical attribution is reported as conditional in the source tradition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece of wood into which the head of a tent-pole is inserted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized tent or construction implement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vessel that is nearly full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine and plural forms are also recorded; the word is connected in the lexical discussion with being near fullness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quantity just short of the full or heaped-up contents of a vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to an amount nearly equal to a vessel’s full measure, not necessarily to the vessel itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land without water or trees, land cleared for sowing, or land that has never been sown or cultivated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjective or noun for uncultivated or prepared land; the cited lexical authorities give somewhat differing descriptions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wooden implement used by a baker to form bread cakes, possibly including a rolling-pin-like tool.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source reports uncertainty over one of the synonymous explanations and over a later explanatory addition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A knot or joint of a reed or cane.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical or material sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dates scattered or remaining among the roots of palm branches after the fruit racemes have been cut.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form كَرَابَةٌ is also recorded as an alternate; the plural is أَكْرِبَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a disputed interpretation of a poetic passage, mountain tops or upper places from which mountain water flows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This interpretation is attributed to one authority and explicitly challenged by another; it should not be treated as the ordinary meaning of كُرَابَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A misfortune, calamity, or severe calamity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine noun with the plural كَرَائِبُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The chief or nearest angels, traditionally identified with the archangels or cherubim.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical tradition gives several possible derivations, including nearness, firmness, and awe; the term is preserved here as a conventional Classical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression مَا بِالدَّارِ كَرَّابٌ: there is no one in the house.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression rather than a general count-noun meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An afflicting, distressing, or oppressive affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use describing an affair or situation as distressing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firm, hard, or compact in make; said of joints, hooves, animals, ropes, buildings, and similar structures.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive usage, sometimes marked as figurative or conjecturally extended; it includes a firmly jointed animal and a strongly made horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels brought to the doors of tents or dwellings in severe cold so that they may be warmed by the smoke.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source also equates the form with مُقْرَبَاتٌ, so the derivation and exact lexical relationship are uncertain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bucket having a كَرَب attached to it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of a bucket fitted with the specialized bucket-rope attachment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Afflicted, distressed, or oppressed by sorrow, grief, or anxiety.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participle describing a person or other affected entity in a state of distress.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Nearness construction covered by the broader approach meaning.
Tightening the shackle is covered by the binding meaning.
Contains both the bucket-rope breaking use and a separate disputed baker-implement expression.
Conflicting lexical readings are preserved in the target meaning.
Pointer to other locations in the entry.
Form III approach meaning equated with the near branch.
Form IV haste or rapid running.
Noun meaning severe grief or distress.
Valley channels or upper valley parts.
Proverbial noun use of turning soil.
Hard hoof as a firm structure.
Firm animals, ropes, buildings, joints, and horses.
Camels brought near tents in severe cold.
Passive participle for one afflicted by grief.

cautions: The approach and nearness branch is explicitly treated in the root-level tradition as related to قُرْب through substitution, rather than as the central strength-and-distress branch.
The reading in lane-unit:krb:28059:g8:main alternates between “to twist” and “to slay.”
The mountain-top interpretation in lane-unit:krb:28075:g1:sub2 is attributed to one authority and rejected by another.

Several specialized senses of مُكْرَبٌ and مُكْرَبَاتٌ are marked in the lexical evidence as figurative, assumed, or possibly related to قَرَبَ; they are retained as reported Classical usages rather than treated as Quranic meanings.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: lane-unit:krb:28059:g8:main preserves an unresolved manuscript-reading difference between قُتِلَ/“to twist” as transmitted in the entry and قَتَلَ/“to slay.”

lane-unit:krb:28075:g1:sub2 contains a disputed interpretation of أَكْرِبَةٍ as mountain tops; it is represented as a reported but non-standard Classical interpretation, not as the ordinary meaning of كُرَابَةٌ.
